profile.name: Tobi Awolaju
profile.title: Engineer · Builder · Researcher
profile.bio:
I build software and systems across infrastructure, blockchain, embedded engineering, and applied research.

Final-year Electrical Engineering student at Adeleke University, graduating July 2027 · Independent builder
Open to global engineering opportunities.

projects.title: World of Nads ↗
projects.description: A web-first 3D multiplayer game with browser and Android builds. I build the Godot client, Rust multiplayer server, and Monad-based game systems.

writeup.hardPart: The main challenge is keeping multiplayer state responsive across browsers and lower-end devices. I profiled the Godot-to-JavaScript boundary, identified expensive per-frame bridge calls, and reworked synchronization around batched network updates.
highlights: Godot 3D client compiled to WebAssembly for browser play
Rust WebSocket server for authoritative multiplayer state
Client-side movement interpolation and server reconciliation
Batched state updates to reduce browser bridge overhead
Monad smart-contract integration for game-related transactions
writeup.stack: Godot, WebAssembly, Rust, Tokio, WebSockets, TypeScript, Solidity, Monad, PostgreSQL, Privy.

projects.title: EEG Communication Headset ↗
projects.description: An experimental wearable communication-support interface using EEG sensing, an ESP32, and audio output. The focus is on detecting useful intentional input, not decoding arbitrary thoughts.

writeup.hardPart: EEG signals are weak and easily affected by eye movement, muscle activity, and electrical noise. The prototype explores reliable signal acquisition and intentional-input detection within the constraints of a low-cost embedded platform.
highlights: Prototype built around NeuroSky TGAM sensing and an ESP32
Firmware parses ThinkGear UART packets and validates checksums
Exploring event-based input and audio feedback
Hardware assembled for bench testing; enclosure and integration work remain
writeup.stack: ESP32, Embedded C/C++, FreeRTOS, NeuroSky TGAM, UART, EEG, audio electronics.

projects.title: Cellular Fingerprint Positioning ↗
projects.description: Final-year Electrical Engineering research investigating position estimation from cellular signal measurements in places where GPS is unreliable or unavailable.

writeup.hardPart: Cellular signal strength varies with buildings, multipath, shadowing, and network conditions. The project investigates fingerprint-based positioning rather than relying on simple distance estimates from signal strength.
highlights: Collecting GSM/LTE signal and cell information
Building multi-cell signal fingerprints
Investigating k-nearest-neighbour and probabilistic matching
Evaluating positioning error across outdoor and indoor areas
writeup.stack: GSM/LTE, cellular modems, AT commands, Python, NumPy, SciPy, k-NN, RF propagation.

projects.title: Know Your Protocol ↗
projects.description: An on-chain accountability platform that lets users make commitments and verify follow-through through wallet activity and smart contracts.

writeup.hardPart: The core challenge was detecting meaningful user activity across EVM protocols without depending on custom event signatures. I built an activity-scanning approach using indexed contract logs and connected it to commitment and verification logic.
highlights: AI-assisted protocol research pipeline
Protocol activity detection using EVM log queries
Solidity commitment contracts with automated verification logic
Backend worker for scheduled commitment checks
Recognized in the BuildAnything Spark Hackathon
writeup.stack: Svelte, TypeScript, Node.js, Solidity, viem, ethers, Firebase, Gemini API, Privy, Monad.

projects.title: Rug Pool ↗
projects.description: A smart-contract experiment where participants are locked in until a defined exit time, with verifiable randomness determining the payout.

writeup.hardPart: The challenge was enforcing exit restrictions at the contract level while making the outcome independently verifiable. I integrated Pyth Entropy and tested the payout flow against edge cases.
highlights: Contract-enforced exit restrictions
Pyth Entropy integration for verifiable randomness
53 passing automated tests reported for the project
writeup.stack: Solidity, Hardhat, Monad, Pyth Entropy, TypeScript, React.
